q: Does ZED certification help an MSME get a cheaper loan?
title: Does ZED certification cut loan costs?
short: Sometimes. ZED certification itself does not lower your interest rate by rule, but some banks and state schemes offer concessions to ZED certified units, and the certificate is credible evidence of energy and environment practices. Check your bank's current circular before counting on a rate cut.
audience: Micro and small manufacturers considering ZED Bronze, Silver or Gold

p: The MSME Sustainable (ZED) Certification Scheme of the Ministry of MSME, relaunched in 2022, certifies units at Bronze, Silver and Gold levels on quality, energy, environment and safety parameters. The ministry subsidises the certification cost, most for micro units (80%), then small (60%) and medium (50%), with extra support for some categories of owners and regions.

sections.h: Where a loan benefit can come from
ul: Bank products: some banks have offered lower processing fees or a small interest concession for ZED certified units. These are bank decisions and change.
State incentives: some state MSME policies have linked support to ZED certification; check your state's current policy.
Credit appraisal: a certified unit has documented processes, which helps a credit officer even with no formal concession.

sections.h: What a green loan needs beyond ZED
p: A green loan under the Green Loan Principles funds a specific eligible project and asks for its expected benefit, such as energy saved and emissions avoided, and reporting after disbursement. ZED shows good practice at the unit; it does not by itself measure a project's savings. Pair it with energy bills before and after, and an estimate of savings.

Go for ZED if the subsidised fee is small for you and your buyers or state scheme value it. Do not go for it only for a rate cut unless your own bank confirms the concession in writing. For a green loan, energy and emissions evidence matters more than the certificate.

senseible: Senseible's green loan readiness check uses energy and emissions records built from your bills and fuel invoices, the same records that support ZED energy and environment parameters. Senseible does not issue or assess ZED certification.
